name: What should I consider when removing a wall to open up a kitchen in an older Denver area home?

mainEntity.name: What should I consider when removing a wall to open up a kitchen in an older Denver area home?

acceptedAnswer.text: In homes across Denver, Centennial, and Parker, open-concept conversions frequently require evaluating whether dividing walls between the kitchen and dining area are load-bearing. Removing load-bearing partitions requires installing engineered beams and temporary structural support to carry ceiling and roof loads safely. In non-bearing partition walls, modifications still require rerouting concealed electrical wiring, plumbing vents, or HVAC ducts into new chases or exterior walls. A contractor experienced in custom framing handles the structural work, drywall patch-in, and ceiling blending so the opened space transitions naturally into adjacent living areas.
acceptedAnswer.description: You must determine if the wall is load-bearing to plan proper beam support, and account for rerouting hidden plumbing, electrical lines, or ductwork inside the partition.
